clips: Skill-set is a folder of playbooks for coding agents. Type a slash command and the agent follows that skill.
Most skills are reusable on any repo. Three of them are wired to my job stack.
Claim-fix, ticket-demo, and explain-implementation need GitLab, demo login, and my product screens. Adjust those before you run them elsewhere.

copy.footer: Adjust claim-fix, ticket-demo, and explain-implementation for another repo.

clips: Fake no more checks every factual claim against a primary source, not against memory.
Each claim is marked confirmed, wrong, or unverifiable, with the source next to it.
Use it when a report states numbers or history. This skill is general — no job login needed.
Claim M-R posts a short note on a pull request so nobody starts the same review twice.
Paste a GitHub, GitLab, or Gitea URL. The agent writes claimed for review and stops.
If someone else already claimed it, the skill does not double-work. This one is general.
Claim-fix ticket is my ticket loop. It claims a GitLab issue and records a red before video of the bug.
Then it implements the fix and records a green after video of the same region.
Job wired. It expects GitLab boards, demo login, and Phoenix locators. Swap those for your project.

copy.footer: Swap GitLab, demo login, and locators for your project.

clips: Ticket demo video is a spoken walkthrough. Eve talks while a real cursor clicks the product.
Length follows the explanation. It is not a fifteen second cap.
Job wired. It uses my Eve assets and a per-repo demo login. Bring your own login if you reuse it.

copy.footer: Bring your own demo login and locators.

clips: Explain implementation is a two-act film. First Eve walks locked decisions on a studio board.
Then a live recording proves the result. Act two is your screen capture, unredacted.
Job wired. Same family as ticket demo. Point it at your host or your own recording.

copy.footer: Use your host or your own .mov.

clips: Explain in browser opens a long answer as a readable HTML page.
The terminal only keeps a short teaser: headline, a few bullets, and the file path.
Use it when a walkthrough would be painful to read in the TUI. This skill is general.
Playwright agent clicks a real browser by name. You say the Sign in button or the Email field.
If it cannot find exactly one match, it stops. It does not guess a CSS selector.
Ticket-demo login and claim-fix highlight already use it. The CLI works on any site.

copy.methodB: Stop if zero or two matches
copy.footer: CLI is reusable. Login helpers may be job-wired.

clips: Install copies every skill into Grok, Claude, and Cursor with one script.
Run install-sh global from the repo. Pass skill name if you only want one.
Start a new session so they appear. Ticket-demo and claim-fix pull playwright-agent automatically.

copy.footer: New session after install. --skill NAME copies one.

clips: Evals grade decisions, not live video. Fixtures catch a wrong skip or a bad claim.
Demo videos stay local. Do not commit mp4 files. Upload them onto the merge request.
Authenticated recordings ask you for a temporary login per project. There is no built-in user.

copy.methodB: Upload to the MR — do not commit
copy.footer: Per-project login. No built-in product user.
